newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo JAT to invest $1bln in fleet renewal by 2005.
newsitem.headline: Yugo JAT to invest $1bln in fleet renewal by 2005.

text.p: Yugoslavia's flag carrier Jugoslovenski aerotransport (JAT) said on Tuesday it planned to invest $1 billion in renewing its fleet by 2005 to meet growing client demands for more comfort and better quality services.
The company also said it would make final decisions on replacing six to eight DC9s and Boeing 727s by the end of 1997.

"We must decide and select planes for Middle-European destinations in 1997, to replace the existing fleet of DC9s and 727s and choose the aircraft supplier we will cooperate with," JAT General Manager Zika Petrovic told Reuters in an interview.

Petrovic said $500 million to $600 million dollars will be invested in buying airplanes while the remaining $400 million to $500 million will be directed to purchase engines, spare parts, equipment, for training and commercial promotion.
JAT in April held talks with representatives of Airbus Industrie on possibilities to rejuvenate its fleet with Airbus planes.

"We held talks with Airbus Industrie who accepted to talk to JAT. Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp have remained on sidelines because of the American political stand. But we still want all suppliers to be equal," Petrovic said.
Petrovic said no final decision will be made before JAT concludes talks with aircraft engine producers as well.
JAT's fleet to be replaced is on the average 22 to 25 years old. Some of the planes have been replaced over the past few years with Boeing 737-300s which are 7-1/2 to 8-1/2 years old.

"We are not commercially and financially strong enough to follow the international trends in renewing the fleet every seven or eight years. But when we renew our fleet it will bring changes in technology, maintenance, flying, training and overall business philosophy," Petrovic said.
Half of JAT's fleet of 35 planes was still financially burdened. DC9s were completely paid for as well as four 727s. But four 727s, three ATRs and 737-300 were not fully paid.

JAT will try to organise funding for new purchases via a consortium of Yugoslav banks, but aircraft suppliers were also expected to secure external credits for the planned purchases, Petrovic said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
